---
format:
  typst:
    papersize: us-letter
    margin:
      x: 1.4cm
      y: 1.4cm
params:
  school: "School A"
  min_n: 10
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

# ---- Item dictionary: raw item -> construct -> short label -> reverse flag ----
# Edit the labels/constructs here; everything downstream is driven off this table.
# Constructs reflect the 3-factor CFA solution (see cfa_3factor.R).
items <- tribble(
  ~item,           ~construct,                   ~label,                        ~reverse,
  "enjoy",         "Interest & self-efficacy",   "Enjoy math this year",         FALSE,
  "interesting",   "Interest & self-efficacy",   "Find it interesting",          FALSE,
  "important",     "Interest & self-efficacy",   "Important to everyday life",   FALSE,
  "math_person",   "Interest & self-efficacy",   "See myself as a math person",  FALSE,
  "can_solve",     "Interest & self-efficacy",   "Can solve math problems",      FALSE,
  "belonging",     "Belonging",                  "Sense of belonging",           FALSE,
  "valued",        "Belonging",                  "Feel like a valued member",    FALSE,
  "comfortable",   "Belonging",                  "Comfortable sharing ideas",    FALSE,
  "many_ways",     "Classroom culture",          "We value many ways",           FALSE,
  "mistakes",      "Classroom culture",          "Mistakes help learning",       FALSE,
  "explain",       "Classroom culture",          "Asked to explain thinking",    FALSE,
  "classmates",    "Classroom culture",          "Classmates have good ideas",   FALSE,
  "teacher_talks", "Classroom culture",          "Teacher does most talking",    TRUE
)

construct_levels <- c("Interest & self-efficacy", "Belonging", "Classroom culture")
construct_cols <- c("Interest & self-efficacy" = "#1D9E75",
                    "Belonging"                = "#D85A30",
                    "Classroom culture"        = "#378ADD")

# ---- Load the cleaned, tidy responses (produced by prep_data.R) ----
# Long format, columns: school, student_id, item, response (1-5).
responses <- readr::read_csv("responses.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# ---- Filter to the school passed in by the render loop ----
school_data <- responses |> filter(school == params$school)
n_students  <- n_distinct(school_data$student_id)

# Fail clearly if the school filter matched nothing, instead of erroring
# deep in the plotting code. Usually means params$school doesn't match a
# value in responses.csv (render via render_all.R, which pulls the school
# names straight from the data), or the school column is blank/NA upstream.
if (nrow(school_data) == 0) {
  stop("No responses for school = '", params$school, "'. ",
       "Available schools: ",
       paste(sort(unique(responses$school)), collapse = ", "))
}

# ---- % agree (top-2-box) per item, with small-cell suppression ----
agree <- school_data |>
  group_by(item) |>
  summarise(n = sum(!is.na(response)),
            pct_agree = mean(response >= 4, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
            .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(items, by = "item") |>
  mutate(
    suppressed = n < params$min_n,
    pct_plot   = ifelse(suppressed, 0, pct_agree),
    pct_label  = ifelse(suppressed, "n too small", paste0(round(pct_agree), "%")),
    label      = ifelse(reverse, paste0(label, " *"), label),
    construct  = factor(construct, levels = construct_levels)
  )

tiles <- agree |>
  filter(!suppressed) |>
  group_by(construct) |>
  summarise(pct = round(mean(pct_agree)), .groups = "drop") |>
  complete(construct = factor(construct_levels, levels = construct_levels)) |>
  mutate(pct_label = ifelse(is.na(pct), "—", paste0(pct, "%")))
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-functions
plot_construct <- function(df, construct_name, fill_col) {
  d <- df |>
    filter(construct == construct_name) |>
    mutate(label = fct_reorder(label, pct_agree))
  ggplot(d, aes(pct_plot, label)) +
    geom_col(fill = fill_col, width = 0.62) +
    geom_text(aes(label = pct_label), hjust = -0.08, size = 3, colour = "grey25") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 118), expand = expansion(0)) +
    labs(title = construct_name, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      panel.grid  = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey20"),
      plot.title  = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11.5),
      plot.margin = margin(4, 8, 4, 4)
    )
}

plot_tiles <- function(t) {
  t <- t |> mutate(construct = factor(construct, levels = construct_levels))
  ggplot(t, aes(1, 1)) +
    geom_text(aes(label = pct_label), size = 9, fontface = "bold", colour = "grey15") +
    facet_wrap(~construct, nrow = 1) +
    theme_void(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      strip.text   = element_text(size = 9.5, face = "bold", colour = "grey30"),
      panel.spacing = unit(1.2, "lines")
    )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-onepager
#| fig-width: 7.4
#| fig-height: 9.4
panels <- imap(construct_cols, ~plot_construct(agree, .y, .x))

# Stack the three constructs vertically; panel heights track item counts
# (Interest & self-efficacy = 5, Belonging = 3, Classroom culture = 5).
layout <- plot_tiles(tiles) /
  panels[["Interest & self-efficacy"]] /
  panels[["Belonging"]] /
  panels[["Classroom culture"]] +
  plot_layout(heights = c(0.8, 5, 3, 5))

layout + plot_annotation(
  title    = paste0(params$school, " \u2014 student math perceptions, spring 2026"),
  subtitle = paste0("n = ", n_students,
                    " students  \u00b7  bars show % who agree or strongly agree (top-2-box)",
                    "  \u00b7  * reverse-coded: high agreement is the less student-centered direction"),
  caption  = "Items with fewer than the minimum responses are suppressed.",
  theme = theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey35"),
    plot.caption  = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey45")
  )
)
```
